newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares mixed, bargain-hunting seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares mixed, bargain-hunting seen.

text.p: Singapore noon stocks stumbled lower on Monday after an initial rebound with China-linked stocks continuing to draw best demand ahead of the handover of Hong Kong.

"Fund managers are said to be pre-occupied with Hong Kong, so regional bourses are not going anywhere," a local bank dealer said. He noted the market was drifting at current levels due to caution over poor fundamentals and lack of incentives.
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was 1.20 points firmer at 1,975.57, but the broader market weaker.
Losers led gainers by 131 to 106 and volume was a light 70 million contracts.
Newly-listed Tianjin Zhongxin Pharmaceutical TIAN.SI was at US$1.18, a new high, up 15 cents, aided by handover euphoria.
China North Industrial also rose to an intraday high of US$0.65, before easing back to US$0.635, up 6.5 cents.
Dealers said early interest in some blue chips appeared to have faded although a few continued to attract investors.
Metro Holdings, was at S$4.66, up 14 cents, but off its high of S$4.76. It reported full year results at S$11.9 million on Friday compared with S$1.1 million previously.
F&N recaptured some lustre, rising 10 cents to S$10.10.
